Arms and legs have continuous meshes with blended two-bone skinning. Torso, head, paws and facial components remain separate authored surfaces.
Eyes, eyelids, nose, mouth and paw digits are modeled geometry, not independently actuated facial muscles or fingers.
The green dragon stays attached to the torso-side anatomical-right shoulder helper; head, tail and wings have local authored controls only.
The golden orb is an authored action prop, not part of the reference portrait. Crafting gestures do not change its geometry or simulate manufacture.
General PBR edition: embedded normal maps, short fur and glossy surfaces have not been reduced to or approved by the Weft diffuse-only profile.
All native glTF transforms are authored meters/Y-up/+Z-front after Blender export; scale is not calibrated to the live simulator.
The neutral pose is arms resting beside the rounded body, feet flat, face forward; it is not an observed simulator pose.
The new continuous head deformation authors the muzzle and chin from visual interpretation; it is not a scan, image-to-mesh recovery or a new face control rig.
Iris and pupil geometry are glossy opaque curved shells. There is no refractive transparent cornea, painted catchlight or eye-tracking behavior.
Every iris uses disk UV0 centered at [0.5,0.5], rim radius 0.5; the central pupil shell covers part of the native radial color texture.
Dragon horn ridges, visible crown scales and thickened curved wing membranes are authored geometry; the remaining scales are procedural surface detail.
No new clip boundary, visual quality or hair-density claim follows from preserving authored keys. Native render and exported-model inspection remain required.
Existing native hair lengths are 1.8 times v1 and ribbon lengths 1.4 times v1. Hair remains static authored grooming following skin weights, without hair dynamics.
The solid three-spike forelock is removed. A low rounded emitter, mostly buried in the existing head, supplies a separate fine crown groom; no bare cone or triangle is used as a hair strand.
The new eye-patch offset is .033m from the authored face surface to cover the longer white head groom. Hair overlap and final facial-line visibility still require rendered inspection.
Panda iris radii are .0715/.0795m and pupil radius is 70% of the iris; dragon iris radii are .0365/.0415m and pupil radius is 72%. Radial UV0 and opaque glossy eye shells remain unchanged in meaning.
The surface plan is 22,020,096 pixels for two channels, plus one 1024-square card atlas per fur material; no external texture acquisition is involved.
The plush lighting and viewer-left camera are authored presentation choices, not a reference-camera calibration. Organic facial form still differs from Muse and no parity is asserted.

The v3 charcoal material changes sRGB color to[0.04,0.038,0.034,1] and existing procedural HD fur strength to0.06. This is an authored look adjustment, not reference-color calibration or a rendered improvement claim.

The fourteen previously bare panda foot/toe/paw-digit surfaces receive606 native parents with30 children, adding18,786 configured fibers and180 exported six-vertex hair cards. Dragon feet and all other surfaces are unchanged.

The complete v3 recipe requests7,688 skinned hair cards and at most238,328 configured native parent/child hairs. Native Blender strands are not exported as GLB hairs, and these counts are not independently counted rendered fibers.

All v2 geometry, existing grooms, ivory/facial materials, UVs, rig, attachments, four clips and presentation settings are preserved. The shorter added contact fur can intersect the unchanged authored floor; it is not contact simulation.
Native hair is authored into directional rest-space curves, retaining the emitter skin; there is no dynamic hair simulation. The GLB contains its separate masked-card coat.

source_edit_prompt: Re-author the Muse-inspired panda as a compact, expressive, complete animated 3D character. Use the supplied Muse portrait for proportions, black-and-ivory palette, warm brown eyes, broad cheeks, soft muzzle, smile and the small green dragon on its anatomical right/viewer-left shoulder. Replace stacked joint balls with continuous weighted arms and legs. Model visible short fur, eyelids, layered glossy eyes, nostrils, mouth crease, ears, paws, toes and a rear tail. The shoulder dragon must have shaped head/body, eyes, nostrils, smile, horns, frills, scaled green skin, segmented belly, claws, curved tail and complete scalloped wings with raised spars. Include all these features in the skinned GLB, not only in the render. Use embedded procedural fur/scale surface textures and opaque physically based materials. Preserve a small golden crafting orb as an explicitly authored action prop. Idle breathes and the dragon nods; making_something rubs and rolls the orb between the paws; working lifts it for inspection; milestone_level_up presents it with a happy arm lift. Author all unseen surfaces, rig, fur placement and motion; do not claim recovered geometry, hair simulation, facial capture, Weft compatibility or exact Muse-quality equivalence.
source_hd_v1_prompt: Refine the existing Muse-inspired, complete animated panda and shoulder dragon as real 3D geometry. Use the supplied Muse portrait for its softly integrated muzzle, curved smile, warm large glossy eyes, slightly pear-shaped eye patches, fine fur and organic small green dragon. Sculpt the panda muzzle into the continuous head surface, not two attached cheek balls. Add shaped nostrils, curved fitted lids and convex warm iris geometry with explicit radial UV0 for native 1024 procedural iris color/normal maps. Preserve physical light reflections instead of painting glints. Give the dragon an integrated snout, a smooth weighted neck, curved tapered horns and frills, raised forehead scales, fitted lids and closed curved scalloped wing membranes with smooth finger spars. Use native 2048 fur surfaces on ivory/charcoal and 1024 scale surfaces on green skin, with bounded 512 secondary surfaces. Preserve all twenty-two bones, existing four motion clips, attachment hierarchy, proportions, framing and orb. Use a bounded fine-fiber cutout-card groom in the GLB and separately editable native Blender hair on matching emitters for native previews; native hairs are not secretly exported as browser hair. This is an authored visual interpretation, not recovered unseen anatomy, measured rigging, Weft runtime acceptance, hair simulation or demonstrated Muse-quality parity.
source_hd_v2_prompt: Refine the preserved Muse-inspired HD panda and its green anatomical-right/viewer-left shoulder dragon after reviewing the actual v1 and dense-fur portraits against the supplied Muse reference. Keep the complete three-dimensional geometry, twenty-two-bone skeleton, attachment hierarchy and all four authored clips. Give the panda a visibly longer, denser fine coat: native parent counts unchanged on existing emitters, thirty interpolated children, length 1.8 times v1 capped at .035m, radius 1.5 times v1 and roughness .0015. Keep exported six-vertex hair ribbons distinct from native hair: length 1.4 times v1, width 1.25 times v1, each capped at .04m. Replace the flat brown inner ears with charcoal-furred surfaces. Remove the three exposed white plastic forelock spikes; use a small buried rounded ivory emitter with fine groomed hair for the crown tuft. Increase the warm radial-UV iris and black pupil shells so the white rim is narrower, while retaining opaque convex glossy depth and real light reflections. Use softly off-white sclera instead of a bright toy-like white ring. Raise the black eye-patch layer enough to cover the lengthened white head groom. Use the plush studio preset and a modest three-quarter camera from viewer-left. Preserve the dragon, crafting orb, palette and motion meaning. These are authored visual changes, not recovered anatomy, hair dynamics, runtime physics or verified Muse-quality parity.
